You are implementing Layer 3 (the final layer) of a stacked-PR setup for a Power Platform demo repo (`rpothin/mcdm26-ai-native-powerplatform-dev`).

This branch sits on top of:
- Layer 1: `.github/skills/` — 4 project-level orchestrator skills (`data-management`, `agent-implementation`, `app-implementation`, `backend-process-implementation`)
- Layer 2: `Makefile` + `.github/workflows/deploy-solution.yml`

Your sole task: **create `AGENTS.md` at the repo root** using the `agents-md-builder` skill.

## Context about this repo

This is a demo companion repository for "AI-Native Power Platform Development: Building from the IDE" (Microsoft Community Days Montreal 2026). It demonstrates an IDE-centred, AI-assisted development workflow for Power Platform.

**Tech stack in use:**
- Power Platform CLI (`pac`) — pinned version `2.9.3+` (tested with `2.10.1`)
- Node.js 22.x + npm 11.x
- Azure CLI (`az`) 2.88.0+
- Azure Developer CLI (`azd`) 1.29.0+
- GitHub CLI (`gh`) 2.96.0+
- gh-stack extension 0.1.0+
- Entire CLI (`entire`) 0.9.0+
- React + Vite (for Power Apps code apps, not yet scaffolded but planned under `code-apps/`)

**Installed Copilot plugins (all project-level):**
- `dataverse@awesome-copilot` (from `microsoft/Dataverse-skills`)
- `copilot-studio@skills-for-copilot-studio` (from `microsoft/skills-for-copilot-studio`)
- `code-apps-preview@power-platform-skills` (from `microsoft/power-platform-skills`)
- `power-automate@power-platform-skills` (from `microsoft/power-platform-skills`)
- `mcs-assistant@copilot-studio-plugin` (from `microsoft/copilot-studio-plugin`)

**Project-level orchestrator skills (now in this repo under `.github/skills/`):**
- `data-management` — use for any Dataverse schema, data, solution, admin, or security task
- `agent-implementation` — use for any Copilot Studio agent authoring, review, testing, or management task
- `app-implementation` — use for any Power Apps code app task (scaffold, add connector, lint, deploy)
- `backend-process-implementation` — use for any Power Automate cloud flow task (create, debug, manage)

**Repo structure (current + planned):**
```
.github/
  skills/               ← 4 orchestrator skills (just added)
  workflows/
    deploy-solution.yml ← solution deployment to production (just added)
agents/                 ← Copilot Studio agent files (cloned via agent-implementation skill)
code-apps/             ← Power Apps code apps (one subfolder per app)
solutions/             ← Unpacked Power Platform solutions (one subfolder per solution)
  <name>/
    deployment-settings.json   ← connection refs + env var values per solution
docs/
  tech-stack-readiness.md
scripts/
  tech-stack-readiness.ps1
Makefile               ← lint/test/build/validate targets (just added)
README.md
```

**Key commands:**
- `make lint` — ESLint across all `code-apps/*/`
- `make test` — unit tests across all `code-apps/*/`
- `make build` — build all `code-apps/*/`
- `make validate` — lint + pac solution pack structural check
- `pac solution pack --folder solutions/<name> --zipfile <output>.zip --processCanvasApps`
- `pac solution unpack --zipfile <input>.zip --folder solutions/<name>`
- `pac code push` — deploy a code app
- `pac auth create` — authenticate PAC CLI to an environment

**Deployment:**
- Dev environment: local `pac auth` (developer's own)
- Production: automated via `.github/workflows/deploy-solution.yml` (OIDC, no long-lived secrets)
- **Never run** `pac solution import` against production manually

**Boundaries (3-tier) to encode:**

✅ Always:
- Work on unpacked solution folders under `solutions/` — never hand-edit packed `.zip` files
- Keep connection references and environment variable values in `solutions/<name>/deployment-settings.json`
- Run `make lint` before `pac code push` for code apps
- Keep generated TypeScript under `src/generated/` untouched — always regenerated by connector skills
- Use the project orchestrator skill that matches the task area (listed above)

⚠️ Ask first:
- Adding a premium Power Platform connector (DLP implications)
- Enabling a flow in a production environment
- Importing a solution to a shared/non-dev environment
- Renaming a solution component's `SchemaName` (breaks downstream references)
- Changing pipeline YAML or deployment workflow

🚫 Never:
- Hand-edit a packed solution `.zip` or the `customizations.xml` inside it
- Commit real connection reference IDs, environment IDs, or service-principal secrets
- Run `pac solution import` against a shared environment from a local machine
- Hand-edit `src/generated/` in code apps
- Author Copilot Studio YAML without first running `copilot-studio-advisor`
- Commit directly to `main` — all changes go through PRs

## Instructions

Invoke the `agents-md-builder` skill to create `AGENTS.md`. The skill is already installed at `~/.copilot/skills/agents-md-builder/`. Follow its workflow:

1. Detect mode: **bootstrap** (no `AGENTS.md` exists yet)
2. Discover facts from the repo — read `package.json` files, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/`, `.github/skills/`, `docs/tech-stack-readiness.md`, `README.md`
3. Draw on the context above plus what you discover in the repo; use the relevant templates from `references/` (this is a Power Platform ALM repo + code app repo + Copilot Studio agent repo — multiple templates apply)
4. Write `AGENTS.md` at the repo root following the non-negotiable rules:
   - Hard cap **300 lines** — aim for under 150
   - Executable commands appear early with real flags
   - Prefer file-scoped commands over full-suite
   - Three-tier boundaries (encoded above)
   - **Skill routing map**: a clear table or list mapping task types to the correct project orchestrator skill
   - **Progressive-disclosure pointers** for the areas that benefit from deeper context (point to `docs/tech-stack-readiness.md` for setup, and stub `agent_docs/` paths for future depth)
   - No file paths that will drift; describe capabilities instead
   - No restating what linters enforce

## Delivery

After creating `AGENTS.md`:

1. **Commit** with message:
   ```
   feat: initialize AGENTS.md for AI-native Power Platform demo repo
   
   Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
   ```
2. **Push** the branch to origin.
3. **Open a PR** targeting `rpothin-feat-makefile-and-deployment-workflow` (the Layer 2 branch) with:
   - Title: `feat: initialize AGENTS.md`
   - Body: a brief summary of what the file covers and why each section was included.

When done, reply with the branch name and PR number.

# AGENTS.md Builder

Produces a lean, deliberately-authored `AGENTS.md` that improves — not degrades — coding-agent performance in the target repository.

## When to activate

- User asks to create / write / bootstrap / scaffold an `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
- User asks to improve, shrink, review, or audit an existing one.
- User reports their coding agent keeps making the same mistakes in a repo and no instructions file exists.

Do **not** activate for README work, GitHub Actions authoring, Copilot Studio agent YAML (`agent.mcs.yml`), or Agent Skill authoring.

## Non-negotiable rules

Enforce without asking. These come from the ETH Zurich 2025 study, the GitHub analysis of 2,500+ files, HumanLayer's practice notes, and the aihero.dev guide.

- **Never auto-generate.** Do not run `/init`, do not dump a template blindly, do not scrape the file tree into the file. Auto-generated `AGENTS.md` files reduce task success by ~3% and inflate cost by >20%.
- **Small is the goal.** Hard cap 300 lines. Aim for under 100. Every line ships in every conversation.
- **Filename is `AGENTS.md`** (plural, uppercase) at the repo root. For monorepos add nested `AGENTS.md` in subpackages — nearest file wins.
- **Executable commands appear early**, with real flags (`pnpm test --filter=api`, `uv run pytest tests/unit -x`), not tool names.
- **Prefer file-scoped commands over full-suite** for iteration speed.
- **State stack with versions** ("React 18 + TypeScript 5.4 + Vite 5"), not just names.
- **Three-tier boundaries**: ✅ Always / ⚠️ Ask first / 🚫 Never.
- **Describe capabilities, not file paths.** Paths go stale and poison context on every request. Say "authentication logic and JWT signing", not "see `src/auth/handlers.ts:42`".
- **Do not restate what a linter enforces.** If ESLint / Ruff / gofmt already forbids it, deleting the rule from `AGENTS.md` reclaims instruction budget.
- **Progressive disclosure.** Long-form details go in `agent_docs/*.md` and are *pointed to* from `AGENTS.md` with a one-line trigger ("read `agent_docs/testing.md` before writing integration tests").
- **Pointers over copies.** Never inline code snippets that will drift.

## Workflow

Follow in order. Each step has a clear stopping condition.

### 1. Detect mode

Look for existing files at the repo root:

- No `AGENTS.md` and no `CLAUDE.md` → **bootstrap mode**.
- `AGENTS.md` exists → **improve mode** if the user asked to improve, **audit mode** if they asked to review/audit.
- `CLAUDE.md` exists but no `AGENTS.md` → offer to migrate (rename + symlink; see `references/symlinks.md`).

State the detected mode back to the user in one sentence before doing anything else.

### 2. Discover facts from the repo (do not guess)

Read only manifests and CI config. Do **not** walk the source tree.

- Node: `package.json` (scripts, engines, packageManager), lockfile identity (`pnpm-lock.yaml` → pnpm, `bun.lockb` → bun, `yarn.lock` → yarn).
- Python: `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `requirements*.txt`, `.python-version`.
- Go: `go.mod`. Rust: `Cargo.toml`. .NET: `*.csproj`, `global.json`. Java/Kotlin: `pom.xml`, `build.gradle*`.
- Terraform: `*.tf`, `.terraform-version`, `versions.tf`.
- CI: `.github/workflows/*.yml` — extract the exact test/build/lint commands the CI actually runs. These are the source of truth for step 4.
- Monorepo signals: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `turbo.json`, `nx.json`, `lerna.json`, multiple `package.json` under `apps/` or `packages/`.

Prefer non-obvious tooling when detected (uv, bun, mise, corepack). Tools mentioned in `AGENTS.md` get used ~160× more often than unmentioned ones.

### 3. Ask 3–5 targeted questions (only for things not derivable)

Use `ask_user`, one question at a time. Only ask what the manifests cannot answer:

1. One-sentence purpose of the project (the "why").
2. What must the agent **never** touch? (secrets, generated files, vendored code, production configs)
3. What requires **asking first**? (migrations, public API changes, dependency bumps)
4. Any non-obvious gotcha that has burned a contributor recently?
5. (Monorepo only) Which package should the agent default to when the user is ambiguous?

Do not ask about tech stack, package manager, or test commands — those come from step 2.

### 4. Draft against the checklist

Pick the closest template as scaffolding (see `references/template-*.md` list under **References** below). Fill each section with real, discovered facts. Enforce order:

1. One-sentence project purpose
2. Commands (file-scoped first, full-suite second)
3. Stack with versions
4. Boundaries (Always / Ask first / Never)
5. Testing expectations (framework + how to run)
6. Git workflow (branch names, commit style, PR conventions) — only if non-default
7. Pointers to `agent_docs/*.md` for anything long

Skip any section the repo doesn't need. An empty section is worse than no section.

### 5. Self-audit before writing

Before showing the draft, run through `references/checklist.md` and `references/anti-patterns.md` mentally. Confirm:

- Line count ≤ 300, ideally ≤ 100.
- No embedded directory listing.
- No prose restating what a linter enforces.
- Every stack entry has a version.
- Every command has flags.
- Boundaries use the three tiers.
- No `file:line` pointers that will rot.

If any check fails, revise before showing.

### 6. Deliver

- **Bootstrap mode**: write `AGENTS.md` at repo root. Then offer, in one message, to (a) create compat symlinks (see `references/symlinks.md`), and (b) scaffold `agent_docs/` with stub files for anything pointed to.
- **Improve mode**: write the new version in place, keep a `AGENTS.md.bak` next to it.
- **Audit mode**: **never rewrite in place**. Produce a diff-style report with concrete replacement text per finding. Group findings by severity (bloat / stale / missing / duplicated-by-linter).

### 7. Stop

Do not chain into "and now let me also write the CI workflow / update the README / …". The skill's job is done when the file is written or the audit report is delivered.

## Gotchas

- **`AGENTS.md` (plural)**, not `AGENT.md`. Some blog posts use the singular; the standard is plural.
- **Symlinks on Windows** require developer mode or admin (`mklink` in cmd). Copy-with-note is a valid fallback — see `references/symlinks.md`.
- **Monorepos**: the *nearest* `AGENTS.md` up the tree wins. Duplicating root content in a nested file is the most common bloat source. Nested files should only contain deltas.
- **Instruction budget**: frontier models reliably follow ~150–200 instructions; the harness already consumes ~50. Count instructions during self-audit, not just lines.
- **"Code style" sections are usually waste** — if a linter/formatter enforces it, delete it. Keep only style rules that no tool can enforce (naming intent, architectural preferences).
- **Do not encode task-specific instructions** ("when fixing bug X, do Y"). Non-universal instructions dilute focus on every unrelated turn. Put those in `agent_docs/` and reference them.
- **CI is the source of truth for commands**, not the README. READMEs drift; CI has to work.
- **When both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` exist and disagree**, treat this as a bug — flag it in audit mode and propose consolidation via symlink.

## References

Load only what applies:

- See `references/checklist.md` when drafting (step 4) or self-auditing (step 5) — good/bad examples per section.
- See `references/anti-patterns.md` when in audit mode or when the existing file looks bloated — the failure modes with concrete rewrites.
- See `references/symlinks.md` when the user wants cross-tool compatibility (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot instructions).
- See `references/template-copilot-studio-agent.md` when the repo contains `agent.mcs.yml`.
- See `references/template-powerapps-codeapp.md` when the repo is a Power Apps code app (React + Vite + `pac code push`, `power.config.json`, `PowerProvider`).
- See `references/template-powerplatform-alm.md` when the repo is a Power Platform ALM / solution management repo (solutions/, pipelines, environment promotion).
- See `references/template-integration-patterns.md` when the repo is a docs-heavy pattern library (many examples under `patterns/` or `examples/`, minimal runtime code).
- See `references/template-generic.md` as fallback when no template fits.

</skill-context>

75. ```
76. ## Boundaries
77. - ✅ Always: run the file-scoped lint + typecheck before proposing a diff.
78. - ✅ Always: keep new modules under `src/` and colocate tests as `*.test.ts`.
79. - ⚠️ Ask first: any change under `src/db/migrations/`, any dependency bump, any change to a public export from `packages/*/index.ts`.
80. - 🚫 Never: commit into `dist/`, `.env*`, `secrets/`, or `vendor/`. Never disable a lint rule inline. Never introduce a new dependency without approval.
81. ```
82. 
83. **Bad**
84. > Be careful with the database and don't break anything important.
85. 
86. Non-actionable, no tiers, agent can't route decisions.
87. 
88. ---
89. 
90. ## 5. Testing
91. 
92. Framework, how to run one test, coverage bar, mocking convention.
93. 
94. **Good**
95. > Vitest with `@testing-library/react`. Run one file with `pnpm test -- path/to/file.test.ts`. Coverage bar: 80% for changed lines (enforced in CI). Mock network with MSW handlers in `src/test/msw/`.
96. 
97. **Bad**
98. > We use tests. Run `npm test`.
99. 
100. ---
101. 
102. ## 6. Git workflow *(only if non-default)*
103. 
104. Include only if the repo deviates from mainstream conventions.
105. 
106. **Include when**: trunk-based with signed commits, conventional commits enforced, PR title format checked in CI, required issue link, etc.
107. 
108. **Skip when**: standard feature-branch + PR, no enforced commit style. Trust the model's defaults.
109. 
110. ---
111. 
112. ## 7. Pointers to `agent_docs/`
113. 
114. **Good**
115. > - Read `agent_docs/running-integration-tests.md` before writing anything under `tests/integration/` (Docker setup + fixture reset).
116. > - Read `agent_docs/dataverse-schema.md` before editing entity models.
117. 
118. **Bad**
119. > See the `agent_docs/` folder for more info.
120. 
121. Every pointer needs a **specific trigger condition**.
122. 
123. ---
124. 
125. ## Self-audit gates (fail-any → revise)
126. 
127. - [ ] File is ≤ 300 lines, ideally ≤ 100.
128. - [ ] Instruction count ≤ 100 (each bullet or imperative sentence counts as one).
129. - [ ] No embedded `tree` output or directory listing.
130. - [ ] No `path/to/file.ts:42` pointers that will rot.
131. - [ ] No prose restating what ESLint / Ruff / gofmt / Prettier already enforces.
132. - [ ] Every stack entry has a version.
133. - [ ] Every command has flags a human would actually type.
134. - [ ] Boundaries use the ✅ / ⚠️ / 🚫 tiers.
135. - [ ] No task-specific instructions ("when fixing bug X…"). Those belong in `agent_docs/`.
136. - [ ] No first-person or second-person voice ("I will", "you should"). Third-person imperative only.
137.

1. # AGENTS.md anti-patterns — with concrete rewrites
2. 
3. Use during **audit mode** and whenever an existing file looks bloated. Each anti-pattern lists the smell, why it hurts, and a concrete rewrite.
4. 
5. ## 1. Auto-generated dump
6. 
7. **Smell**: file was created by `/init`, an "explain this repo" prompt, or a codegen script. Reads like a README with sections for everything.
8. 
9. **Why it hurts**: ETH Zurich 2025 study — auto-generated files reduce task success by ~3% and inflate token cost by >20%. Agents follow every instruction; irrelevant ones distract on every unrelated turn.
10. 
11. **Rewrite**: delete the whole file, restart in bootstrap mode, ask the human the 3–5 questions in `SKILL.md` step 3.
12. 
13. ---
14. 
15. ## 2. Directory listing / codebase overview
16. 
17. **Smell**:
18. ```
19. ## Project structure
20. - src/
21.   - auth/
22.     - handlers.ts   ← JWT signing
23.     - middleware.ts
24.   - db/
25.     - client.ts
26. ...
27. ```
28. 
29. **Why it hurts**: paths change constantly. Stale paths *actively* mislead the agent — it will confidently look in the wrong file. Also: the paper shows overviews don't help navigation speed at all.
30. 
31. **Rewrite**: describe **capabilities**, not paths.
32. > The service exposes an HTTP API (Fastify), talks to Postgres via Drizzle, and handles JWT auth. Background jobs run on BullMQ.
33. 
34. ---
35. 
36. ## 3. Restating linter rules
37. 
38. **Smell**:
39. ```
40. - Use 2-space indentation
41. - Semicolons required
42. - Single quotes for strings
43. - Max line length 100
44. - Prefer const over let
45. ```
46. 
47. **Why it hurts**: burns instruction budget for zero benefit — the linter/formatter enforces this deterministically, and LLMs in-context-learn style from existing files anyway.
48. 
49. **Rewrite**: delete. If it matters, add one line:
50. > Prettier + ESLint are authoritative for style. Run `pnpm lint --fix` before proposing a diff.
51. 
52. ---
53. 
54. ## 4. Inlined code snippets
55. 
56. **Smell**: 40 lines of "here's an example component" pasted into `AGENTS.md`.
57. 
58. **Why it hurts**: snippets drift. When the real code evolves, the snippet lies, and the agent copies the lie.
59. 
60. **Rewrite**: point to a real, canonical file that the CI would fail on if it broke:
61. > Follow the shape of `packages/ui/src/Button/Button.tsx` for new components — it's the reference the design system audits against.
62. 
63. ---
64. 
65. ## 5. Task-specific instructions
66. 
67. **Smell**:
68. ```
69. When implementing the checkout flow, remember to call `trackConversion()` after payment success.
70. When fixing issue #482, apply the workaround in `services/payments/`.
71. ```
72. 
73. **Why it hurts**: `AGENTS.md` ships on **every** turn. A checkout-specific rule distracts every documentation, refactor, and test-writing turn.
74. 
75. **Rewrite**: move to `agent_docs/checkout-flow.md` and add one pointer with a trigger condition:
76. > Read `agent_docs/checkout-flow.md` before editing anything under `src/checkout/`.
77. 
78. ---
79. 
80. ## 6. Vague boundaries
81. 
82. **Smell**:
83. > Be careful with production configs. Don't break the build.
84. 
85. **Why it hurts**: unactionable. The agent has no way to route a decision through this.
86. 
87. **Rewrite**: three-tier, concrete.
88. ```
89. - 🚫 Never edit `config/production.*`, `.env*`, or `terraform/environments/prod/`.
90. - ⚠️ Ask first before any change to `Dockerfile` or CI workflows.
91. - ✅ Always run `pnpm typecheck` before proposing a diff.
92. ```
93. 
94. ---
95. 
96. ## 7. Duplicated content in nested `AGENTS.md`
97. 
98. **Smell**: monorepo with `AGENTS.md` at root **and** in each `apps/*/`, each restating the same tech stack and commands.
99. 
100. **Why it hurts**: nested files are *additive* to the nearest — you're shipping the intro twice, and any drift between them becomes contradictory instructions.
101. 
102. **Rewrite**: nested files contain only **deltas**:
103. > This app extends the repo-root `AGENTS.md`. Overrides for this package:
104. > - Package manager: `bun` (not pnpm — legacy).
105. > - Test command: `bun test`.
106. > - 🚫 Never regenerate `src/generated/` — it comes from an upstream schema push.
107. 
108. ---
109. 
110. ## 8. Wall of "always" without any "never"
111. 
112. **Smell**: 15 things the agent should do, zero prohibitions.
113. 
114. **Why it hurts**: the highest-leverage line in the file is usually a prohibition. GitHub's 2,500-repo analysis found "Never commit secrets" was the single most impactful constraint.
115. 
116. **Rewrite**: force at least 2–3 concrete `🚫 Never` items. If the human can't name any, that itself is a signal to ask harder.
117. 
118. ---
119. 
120. ## 9. Task-log / changelog inside `AGENTS.md`
121. 
122. **Smell**:
123. ```
124. ## Recent changes
125. - 2025-03-12: migrated from Yarn to pnpm
126. - 2025-04-01: added Redis for session storage
127. ```
128. 
129. **Why it hurts**: changelogs belong in git history. Every entry ships on every turn forever.
130. 
131. **Rewrite**: delete. If a migration is *in progress* and the agent needs to know, add one line in the current stack section:
132. > Storage is migrating from Redis to Postgres — new code should target Postgres; old Redis paths under `src/legacy-cache/` are frozen.
133. 
134. ---
135. 
136. ## 10. First- or second-person voice
137. 
138. **Smell**:
139. > I want you to always write tests. You should never commit without running the linter.
140. 
141. **Why it hurts**: the file is injected into a system-prompt-adjacent slot. Point-of-view drift degrades routing and instruction-following.
142. 
143. **Rewrite**: third-person imperative.
144. > Always write tests for new modules. Never commit without running the linter.
145.

1. # Makefile — local developer tooling for Power Apps code apps and Power Platform solutions.
2. # Targets operate on directories discovered at runtime so no file changes are needed when
3. # new apps/solutions are added.
4. 
5. # Discover all first-level subdirectories of code-apps/ (each is one Code App workspace).
6. CODE_APPS := $(shell find code-apps -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d 2>/dev/null)
7. 
8. # Discover all first-level subdirectories of solutions/ (each is one unpacked solution).
9. SOLUTIONS := $(shell find solutions -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d 2>/dev/null)
10. 
11. .PHONY: help lint test build validate
12. 
13. ## help: list available targets with descriptions (default)
14. help:
15. 	@echo ""
16. 	@echo "Available targets:"
17. 	@echo "  lint      Run ESLint for every code app under code-apps/"
18. 	@echo "  test      Run unit tests for every code app under code-apps/"
19. 	@echo "  build     Build every code app under code-apps/"
20. 	@echo "  validate  Run lint + pac solution pack (structural check) for every solution"
21. 	@echo ""
22. 
23. ## lint: run 'npm run lint' inside each code app directory
24. lint:
25. 	@if [ -z "$(CODE_APPS)" ]; then \
26. 		echo "No code apps found under code-apps/ — skipping lint."; \
27. 	else \
28. 		# Iterate; `set -e` makes the sub-shell exit on first failure, propagating to make. \
29. 		for app in $(CODE_APPS); do \
30. 			echo "==> Linting $$app"; \
31. 			(cd $$app && npm run lint); \
32. 		done; \
33. 	fi
34. 
35. ## test: run 'npm test' inside each code app directory
36. test:
37. 	@if [ -z "$(CODE_APPS)" ]; then \
38. 		echo "No code apps found under code-apps/ — skipping tests."; \
39. 	else \
40. 		for app in $(CODE_APPS); do \
41. 			echo "==> Testing $$app"; \
42. 			(cd $$app && npm test); \
43. 		done; \
44. 	fi
45. 
46. ## build: run 'npm run build' inside each code app directory
47. build:
48. 	@if [ -z "$(CODE_APPS)" ]; then \
49. 		echo "No code apps found under code-apps/ — skipping build."; \
50. 	else \
51. 		for app in $(CODE_APPS); do \
52. 			echo "==> Building $$app"; \
53. 			(cd $$app && npm run build); \
54. 		done; \
55. 	fi
56. 
57. ## validate: run lint, then verify each solution can be packed by PAC CLI
58. validate: lint
59. 	@# Check PAC CLI availability before iterating to give a clear error message.
60. 	@if ! command -v pac >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
61. 		echo "pac CLI not found — skipping solution pack check. Install from https://aka.ms/PowerAppsCLI"; \
62. 		exit 0; \
63. 	fi
64. 	@if [ -z "$(SOLUTIONS)" ]; then \
65. 		echo "No solutions found under solutions/ — skipping solution pack check."; \
66. 	else \
67. 		for sol in $(SOLUTIONS); do \
68. 			echo "==> Packing $$sol (structural check)"; \
69. 			# Pack to a temp zip; delete immediately — we only care that it succeeds. \
70. 			tmp=$$(mktemp /tmp/pack-XXXXXX.zip); \
71. 			pac solution pack --folder "$$sol" --zipfile "$$tmp" --processCanvasApps; \
72. 			rm -f "$$tmp"; \
73. 		done; \
74. 	fi
75.

1. # mcdm26-ai-native-powerplatform-dev
2. 
3. Demo companion repository for [**AI-Native Power Platform Development: Building from the IDE**, prepared for **Microsoft Community Days Montreal 2026**](https://www.communitydays.org/event/2026-08-21/microsoft-community-days-montreal#sessions?id=1236475).
4. 
5. This repository is the working space for presentation-aligned demonstrations that show how Power Platform work can move from a browser-first experience to an **AI-native, IDE-centered workflow**. The goal is not to prove that one tool replaces every other tool. The goal is to show where AI-assisted development fits, where review gates still matter, and how to structure the work so the results stay reliable.

14. - why teams may want an IDE-centered workflow

16. - where AI agents help across the delivery lifecycle
17. - which review, approval, and ALM gates should remain human-controlled

21. The current working stack includes:

23. - [**GitHub Copilot App**](https://github.com/features/ai/github-app) and [**GitHub Copilot**](https://github.com/features/copilot)

1. # deploy-solution.yml
2. #
3. # PURPOSE
4. # -------
5. # Deploys updated Power Platform solutions to the production environment
6. # whenever changes to `solutions/**` are pushed to the `main` branch.
7. # Each changed solution is packed from its unpacked folder and imported
8. # via the PAC CLI using an OIDC-based auth flow (no long-lived secrets).
9. #
10. # AZURE AD SETUP REQUIRED
11. # -----------------------
12. # 1. Create an App Registration in Azure AD (Entra ID).
13. # 2. Under "Certificates & secrets → Federated credentials", add a credential:
14. #      - Scenario : GitHub Actions deploying Azure resources
15. #      - Organization: rpothin
16. #      - Repository : mcdm26-ai-native-powerplatform-dev
17. #      - Entity     : Branch
18. #      - Branch name: main
19. #    This allows the workflow to exchange the GitHub OIDC token for an Azure
20. #    access token without storing a client secret anywhere.
21. # 3. Grant the App Registration access to the target Power Platform environment
22. #    (System Administrator or equivalent security role).
23. #
24. # REPOSITORY SECRETS (Settings → Secrets → Actions)
25. # ---------------------------------------------------
26. #   AZURE_CLIENT_ID       – Application (client) ID of the App Registration
27. #   AZURE_TENANT_ID       – Azure AD tenant ID
28. #   AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID – Azure subscription ID
29. #
30. # REPOSITORY VARIABLES (Settings → Variables → Actions)
31. # ------------------------------------------------------
32. #   PROD_ENVIRONMENT_URL  – Production Power Platform environment URL
33. #                           e.g. https://org1234abcd.crm.dynamics.com
34. #
35. # DEPLOYMENT SETTINGS PER SOLUTION
36. # ---------------------------------
37. # Each solution folder must contain a `deployment-settings.json` file that
38. # maps environment-specific connection references and environment variables.
39. # Generate a template from an existing packed zip:
40. #   pac solution create-settings --solution-zip <file>.zip --settings-file deployment-settings.json
41. 
42. on:
43.   push:
44.     branches: [main]
45.     paths: ['solutions/**']
46. 
47. permissions:
48.   id-token: write  # Required for OIDC token exchange with Azure AD
49.   contents: write  # Required for gh release create/edit/delete
50. 
51. jobs:
52.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53.   # Job 1: detect — find which solution folders changed in this push
54.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
55.   detect:
56.     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
57.     outputs:
58.       solutions: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.solutions }}
59. 
60.     steps:
61.       - name: Checkout
62.         uses: actions/checkout@v4
63.         with:
64.           fetch-depth: 2  # Need HEAD and HEAD~1 to compute the diff
65. 
66.       - name: Detect changed solutions
67.         id: changed
68.         run: |
69.           # List files that changed between the previous commit and this one,
70.           # filter to paths inside solutions/, extract the solution name (second
71.           # path segment), deduplicate, then encode as a JSON array.
72.           CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD -- 'solutions/' \
73.             | sed 's|solutions/\([^/]*\)/.*|\1|' \
74.             | sort -u)
75. 
76.           if [ -z "$CHANGED" ]; then
77.             echo "solutions=[]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
78.           else
79.             # Build a JSON array from the newline-delimited list.
80.             JSON=$(echo "$CHANGED" | jq -R . | jq -sc .)
81.             echo "solutions=$JSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
82.           fi
83. 
84.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
85.   # Job 2: deploy — pack and import each changed solution
86.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87.   deploy:
88.     needs: detect
89.     if: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.solutions != '[]' && needs.detect.outputs.solutions != '' }}
90. 
91.     strategy:
92.       matrix:
93.         solution: ${{ fromJson(needs.detect.outputs.solutions) }}
94.       fail-fast: false  # Let independent solutions proceed even if one fails
95. 
96.     environment: production  # Enables GitHub environment protection rules
97.     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
98. 
99.     steps:
100.       - name: Checkout
101.         uses: actions/checkout@v4
102. 
103.       - name: Install PAC CLI
104.         uses: microsoft/powerplatform-actions/install-pac-cli@v1
105. 
106.       - name: Create release candidate
107.         id: create_release
108.         env:
109.           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
110.         run: |
111.           SHORT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
112.           TAG="${{ matrix.solution }}-v${SHORT_SHA}-rc"
113.           gh release create "$TAG" \
114.             --prerelease \
115.             --title "${{ matrix.solution }} RC-${SHORT_SHA}" \
116.             --notes "Automated release candidate for ${{ matrix.solution }}"
117.           echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
118. 
119.       - name: Pack solution
120.         run: |
121.           mkdir -p dist
122.           pac solution pack \
123.             --folder "solutions/${{ matrix.solution }}" \
124.             --zipfile "dist/${{ matrix.solution }}.zip" \
125.             --processCanvasApps
126. 
127.       - name: Azure login (OIDC)
128.         uses: azure/login@v2
129.         with:
130.           client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
131.           tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
132.           subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
133. 
134.       - name: Authenticate PAC CLI
135.         run: |
136.           # Exchange the Azure session token for a Power Platform-scoped token,
137.           # then register the auth context so subsequent pac commands target the
138.           # correct environment without storing credentials in the workflow.
139.           TOKEN=$(az account get-access-token \
140.             --resource "https://service.powerapps.com/" \
141.             --query accessToken -o tsv)
142.           pac auth create \
143.             --environment "${{ vars.PROD_ENVIRONMENT_URL }}" \
144.             --token "$TOKEN"
145. 
146.       - name: Import solution
147.         id: import
148.         continue-on-error: false
149.         run: |
150.           pac solution import \
151.             --path "dist/${{ matrix.solution }}.zip" \
152.             --deploymentSettingsFile "solutions/${{ matrix.solution }}/deployment-settings.json" \
153.             --activate-plugins \
154.             --force-overwrite \
155.             --publish-changes
156. 
157.       - name: Promote release on success
158.         if: steps.import.outcome == 'success'
159.         env:
160.           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
161.         run: |
162.           TAG="${{ steps.create_release.outputs.tag }}"
163.           gh release edit "$TAG" --prerelease=false --latest
164. 
165.       - name: Rollback release on failure
166.         if: failure() && steps.create_release.outcome == 'success'
167.         env:
168.           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
169.         run: |
170.           TAG="${{ steps.create_release.outputs.tag }}"
171.           gh release delete "$TAG" --yes
172.           # Remove the tag from the remote; ignore errors if it was never pushed.
173.           git push origin --delete "$TAG" || true
174.

1. # Tech stack readiness (demo replay)

3. This page captures the setup and validation flow used to prepare this repository for the demo stack.
4.

2. name: agent-implementation
3. description: >
4.   Orchestrates Copilot Studio agent work in the mcdm26 Power Platform demo project,
5.   routing across the two installed Copilot Studio plugin sets: `copilot-studio`
6.   (microsoft/skills-for-copilot-studio) and `mcs-assistant`
7.   (microsoft/copilot-studio-plugin). Use for any task involving Copilot Studio agents:
8.   cloning, describing, designing topics/actions/knowledge, authoring YAML, pushing,
9.   publishing, and testing. Triggers on: build agent, create topic, add knowledge source,

# AGENTS.md

Demo companion repo for "AI-Native Power Platform Development: Building from the IDE" (Microsoft Community Days Montreal 2026) — demonstrates an IDE-centred, AI-assisted workflow spanning Copilot Studio agents, Power Apps code apps, and Power Platform solution ALM.

## Commands

File-scoped (prefer for fast feedback):

```sh
npm run lint -- <path>   # lint one file inside a code app directory
npm test -- <path>       # test one file inside a code app directory
npx tsc --noEmit <path>  # typecheck one file
```

Full suite (only when asked):

```sh
make lint      # ESLint across all code-apps/*/
make test      # unit tests across all code-apps/*/
make build     # build all code-apps/*/
make validate  # make lint + pac solution pack structural check for every solution under solutions/
```

Solution pack / unpack:

```sh
pac solution unpack --zipfile <file>.zip --folder solutions/<name>
pac solution pack   --folder solutions/<name> --zipfile <file>.zip --processCanvasApps
```

Other:

```sh
pac auth create --environment <env-url>  # authenticate PAC CLI to a target environment
pac code push                            # deploy a code app (run make lint first)
```

## Stack

- Power Platform CLI (`pac`) 2.9.3+ (tested 2.10.1)
- Node.js 22.x · npm 11.x
- Azure CLI 2.88.0+ · Azure Developer CLI (`azd`) 1.29.0+
- GitHub CLI 2.96.0+ · gh-stack 0.1.0+ · Entire CLI 0.9.0+
- Code apps: React + Vite (planned under `code-apps/`, not yet scaffolded)
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions with OIDC auth — no long-lived secrets in workflow

## Skill routing

Always invoke the matching project-level orchestrator skill — never implement cross-skill work by hand:

| Task area | Skill |
|---|---|
| Dataverse schema, records, solutions, security, environment admin | `data-management` |
| Copilot Studio agent authoring, review, testing, ALM | `agent-implementation` |
| Power Apps code app (scaffold, connectors, lint, deploy) | `app-implementation` |
| Power Automate cloud flows (create, debug, manage) | `backend-process-implementation` |

## Boundaries

- ✅ Always: work on unpacked solution folders under `solutions/` — never touch packed `.zip` files directly.
- ✅ Always: keep connection references and environment variable values in `solutions/<name>/deployment-settings.json`.
- ✅ Always: run `make lint` before `pac code push` for code apps.
- ✅ Always: leave generated TypeScript under `src/generated/` untouched — connector skills regenerate it.
- ✅ Always: all changes go through PRs — never commit directly to `main`.
- ⚠️ Ask first: adding a premium Power Platform connector (DLP policy implications).
- ⚠️ Ask first: enabling a flow in a production environment.
- ⚠️ Ask first: importing a solution to any shared or non-dev environment.
- ⚠️ Ask first: renaming a solution component's `SchemaName` — breaks downstream references.
- ⚠️ Ask first: editing `.github/workflows/deploy-solution.yml` or any other pipeline YAML.
- 🚫 Never: hand-edit a packed solution `.zip` or the `customizations.xml` inside it.
- 🚫 Never: commit real connection reference IDs, environment IDs, or service-principal secrets.
- 🚫 Never: run `pac solution import` against a shared environment from a local machine.
- 🚫 Never: hand-edit anything under `src/generated/` in code apps.
- 🚫 Never: author Copilot Studio YAML without first routing through the `agent-implementation` skill (enforces advisor-before-author).

## Progressive-disclosure pointers

- Read `docs/tech-stack-readiness.md` before setting up the toolchain or validating installed versions — it covers exact baseline versions and the automated readiness script.
- Read `agent_docs/environments.md` (stub — create when environment map is documented) before touching environment-specific config or deployment settings.
- Read `agent_docs/pipelines.md` (stub — create when pipeline docs are ready) before modifying the deployment workflow.

## What this PR adds

`AGENTS.md` at the repo root — the instruction file that coding agents (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) read on every turn to orient themselves in this repository.

## Why each section was included

| Section | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **One-sentence purpose** | Role-anchors every agent turn; prevents off-topic work. |
| **Commands** | File-scoped variants first (fast feedback loop for code apps), full-suite second. Sourced from the `Makefile` and CI — not from the README, which can drift. |
| **Stack with versions** | Exact version pins drive which APIs the agent picks; omitting them causes hallucinated API usage. |
| **Skill routing map** | The four project-level orchestrator skills (`.github/skills/`) are the primary work-routing mechanism; encoding them here ensures the agent always delegates to the right skill rather than implementing cross-area work by hand. |
| **Boundaries (3-tier)** | Concrete ✅ / ⚠️ / 🚫 rules so the agent can route decisions without asking. Covers the most critical ALM and security constraints for a Power Platform repo. |
| **Progressive-disclosure pointers** | Keeps `AGENTS.md` lean while pointing to `docs/tech-stack-readiness.md` for setup details and stubbing `agent_docs/` paths for pipeline and environment docs that don't exist yet. |

## What was intentionally omitted

- No directory listing — paths go stale and mislead agents.
- No code-style rules — ESLint/Prettier already enforce those.
- No testing section — no test framework is wired yet (code apps not scaffolded); adding a stub would add noise with zero signal.

## File stats

80 lines — well under the 150-line target and the 300-line hard cap.
